title: Dressing up: Claudell, Gonzell Motts and Lil Armstrong's mother
summary: Patrons dressed up; Hunter paid a lot for her clothes, and Lil Armstrong's mother thought Lil too good for Louis.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did people really dress up to go to those places?

Yes, they did then. Yes. They dressed up to come then, because there was a girl named Claudell, boy that girl wore some clothes. Her mother used to make them. I think her mother was a dressmaker. Claudell, and a girl named Gonzell Motts, they were the models, more or less. And everybody would watch and see what they had on. And I don't like to sound like I'm boasting, but you want me to tell you -- want me to tell you this? They used to say I wore such smart clothes, you know.

Yeah? Well, I don't know, I hope they don't think I'm boasting, but I paid a lot of money for my clothes. And I would wear the smartest clothes. And of course old Claudell and them dressed, so I had to outdress them, you know.

I was just going to say, and Lil Armstrong, she wore some clothes. Lil paid I think more money for her clothes than we did. Yeah, she wore -- she was clothes conscious. She spent a lot of money. In fact, Lil didn't have to bother about money, because her mother was crazy about her, you know, and she took more or less care of her. So Lil's mother -- and Lil's mother thought she was too good for Louis, you know. She didn't want Lil to marry Louis.
No, indeed. She had a fit when she heard that Lil was going to marry Louis. But Louis was a good boy. There wasn't nothing wrong with Louis.
